entry.title: GRC, Trade and Tax in SAP Cloud ERP 2608
entry.content:
Hello Experts,

I'm excited to share the update regarding our latest release - GRC, Trade and Tax in SAP Cloud ERP 2608. This update highlights many significant innovations from SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, and SAP International Trade.

Below, you’ll find a curated selection of release highlights from our core product management team. Before diving in, I invite you to watch the release highlights video.

Video 1. Release Highlight Video for GRC, Trade and Tax in SAP Cloud ERP 2608

This blog covers the following innovations:

SAP Document and Reporting Compliance

  • Data from external systems for VAT returns
  • E-Invoicing Submission Error Resolution Agent​
  • Statutory Report Analysis Agent

SAP International Trade​

  • Low Weight Reporting for Intrastat Declarations​​
  • Check Payments for Trade Compliance Using Global Trade Services​
  • International Trade Classification Agent

SAP Watchlist Screening

  • Integration of SAP Build Work Zone

SAP Document and Reporting Compliance

Data from External Systems for VAT Returns

For businesses with distributed landscapes or those using specialized line-of-business solutions, this release enables the creation of VAT Returns that include tax items from external systems, beginning with the United Kingdom.

Using the manage external tax items app, business users can review, enrich, and upload data from other systems via manual creation or Microsoft Excel. This allows for the generation of a consolidated VAT return, enabling a smoother, more standardized VAT group reporting process that can scale to a single global solution.

 

Video 2. Data from External Systems for VAT Returns

E-Invoicing Submission Error Resolution Agent

As more countries adopt mandatory e-invoicing, rejections from tax authorities can delay order-to-cash processes. This release introduces an agent to simplify and accelerate error correction.

The E-Invoicing Submission Error Resolution Agent classifies and analyzes technical error messages from tax authorities, providing guided root cause analysis and recommended resolution actions in context.

This accelerates error detection, helps organizations meet submission deadlines, and reduces the risk of non-compliance penalties through standardized guidance.

 

Video 3. E-Invoicing Submission Error Resolution Agent

Statutory Report Analysis Agent

Reviewing statutory reports like VAT returns can be time intensive. To address this, a new agent analyzes trends, detects outliers, and performs root cause analysis before submission.

By comparing key figures across reporting periods, the agent identifies irregularities and flags report runs that require attention. It then provides consolidated summaries and actionable recommendations. This helps reduce the time required to review reports, identify potential compliance risks earlier in the process, and enable more informed decision-making.

Image 1. Statutory Report Analysis Agent

SAP International Trade

Low Weight Reporting for Intrastat Declarations

This release enhances Intrastat declaration processing by enabling precise mass entry for very light products. You can now enter weights below one gram for individual Intrastat declaration items, capturing the true product mass without rounding. This improves data quality and compliance, reduces correction requests, and eliminates the need for workarounds. The ability to perform mass updates across declaration items further speeds up maintenance and enhances auditability.

Image 2. Low Weight Reporting for Intrastat Declarations

Check Payments for Trade Compliance Using Global Trade Services

To further strengthen compliance, we have extended sanction party list screening to include bank master data. This feature integrates with SAP Global Trade Services to automatically block payments when a sanction party list or embargo violation is detected for vendors, customers, or their associated banks.

This capability reduces compliance risk by preventing payments to sanctioned parties, strengthens end-to-end trade compliance in one integrated process, and avoids manual review efforts through automated payment blocking.

Image 3. Check Payments for Trade Compliance Using Global Trade Services

International Trade Classification Agent

This release introduces an AI-powered international trade classification agent. This innovation helps product classification specialists by automating the classification of goods for international shipping. It analyzes product characteristics and trade regulations to recommend customs tariff numbers and commodity codes, providing a clear rationale for each recommendation to support easier review and approval.

This saves valuable time, helps ensure compliance, and reduces risk by minimizing manual errors through a robust and auditable decision process.

 

Video 4. International Trade Classification Agent

SAP Watchlist Screening

Integration of SAP Build Work Zone

To simplify access to critical applications, this release integrates SAP Build Work Zone, standard edition with SAP Watch List Screening. This allows you to create a single, common launchpad, grouping together tiles from SAP Watch List Screening and other applications.

This provides business users with a central point of access for all their apps and tasks, delivering an intuitive, role-based, and personalized business site that enhances the user experience and simplifies daily operations.

Image 4. Integration of SAP Build Work Zone

entry.title: What Slovakia's 2027 E-Invoicing Mandate Means for SAP Customers
entry.content:
Slovakia has set its date. From 1 January 2027, if you are a Slovak VAT payer sending a domestic invoice to another business or to a public body, that invoice has to be a structured electronic document. The data goes to the Financial Directorate.

One piece of news first, because it changes what your options look like. SAP is now accredited in the Slovak jurisdiction and appears on the Financial Administration's published list of accredited service providers. Slovakia is not building a central portal. Invoices travel through certified delivery services instead, so the provider you use has to be on that list.

ℹ️ Important info upfront:  if you want to see and hear how SAP plans to support, join us for the webinar on Sept 22 at 10 am CEST   ➡️ register here

What actually changes

The legal basis is the amendment to Act No. 222/2004 on VAT, which took effect on 1 January 2026. The e-invoicing obligation itself starts a year later, on 1 January 2027, and it applies to every VAT payer in the Slovak Republic.

From that date a PDF no longer counts. Invoices have to be structured and compliant with EN 16931, and Slovakia will use a CIUS in scope of the Peppol BIS 3.0 format.

There is one detail in the legislation that is easy to skip past. The recipient's consent for receiving an e-invoice may no longer be required. If your current process asks customers whether they accept electronic invoices, that step may simply fall away.

Two phases, not one

The reform is designed to replace the VAT Control Statement and the EC Sales List, but it does not do that immediately.

Phase 1 starts on 1 January 2027. Mandatory e-invoicing applies to domestic B2B and B2G transactions where the supplier is a Slovak VAT payer. Suppliers issue the structured invoice and report the data to the Financial Directorate. Everything outside that scope still runs through the VAT Control Statement and the EC Sales List, which stay mandatory.

That overlap is worth planning for. In 2027 you are running the new obligation and the old reporting side by side.

Phase 2 starts on 1 July 2030. E-invoicing becomes the default for all B2B and B2G transactions, intra-Community supplies included. The full real-time Digital Reporting Requirement goes live, and the VAT Control Statement and EC Sales List are repealed.

The three moving parts

1️⃣The electronic invoice is a structured document compliant with EN 16931.

2️⃣The delivery service is a certified service that transmits the invoice and reports the required data to the Financial Directorate automatically. This is the accredited provider layer, and it is what makes the Slovak model decentralised.

3️⃣The Digital Reporting Requirement (DRR) covers both sides of the transaction. Suppliers report, and so do recipients. Projects that scope only the outbound side end up doing the work twice.

Three things worth a second look

  • Input VAT deduction on domestic transactions may become conditional on holding a valid electronic invoice. That moves this out of the compliance box and into cash flow.
  • The deadline for issuing an invoice drops from 15 days to 10 days from the taxable event. This applies from 1 July 2030, not from 2027.
  • Invoices need new mandatory content, including the supplier's bank account details and, on corrective documents, a reference to the original invoice.

Where SAP delivery stands today

SAP plans to supports leveraging SAP Document and Reporting Compliance (link). For current planned delivery dates and scope, please refer to SAP Regulatory Change Manager, requirement GSREQEE-10396 for Slovakia (link: https://app.main.regulatory-change-manager.cloud.sap/index.html#/detail/GSREQEE-10396)

For planned timelines, please access tab ‘Product Impact’ and always refer back to this page for  updates. 

What's next for you

  • Check your product and release against the dates above.
  • Scope the inbound side as well as the outbound side.
  • Look at your partner and tax master data. Structured formats surface gaps that a PDF process never exposed.
  • Subscribe to RCM Slovakia Mandate GSREQEE-10396 so delivery changes come to you instantly. 
  • Come to the session: SAP is running a Slovakia readiness update on 22 September 2026 at 10:00 CEST. The session covers where delivery stands, how the phased rollout works in practice, and there is a live demo of SAP Document and Reporting Compliance handling the requirement end to end. It is recorded, so registering gets you the replay if the time does not work for you ➡️ Register here

 

More information: 
SAP Document and Reporting Compliance Page https://www.sap.com/products/financial-management/document-reporting-compliance.html 

Solution Brief https://www.sap.com/products/financial-management/document-reporting-compliance.html?pdf-asset=2221c... 

DRC Community https://pages.community.sap.com/topics/document-reporting-compliance

entry.title: Introducing the Manage Electronic Documents App for Türkiye in SAP Document and Reporting Compliance
entry.content:
Introducing the Manage Electronic Documents App for Türkiye in SAP Document and Reporting Compliance

If you manage electronic documents in Türkiye using SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, you are probably already familiar with the eDocument Cockpit.

The Manage Electronic Documents app provides an SAP Fiori-based user experience for electronic document processing in Türkiye. It includes status overview, visual process flows, a dedicated document details view, and Error Analysis.

How Manage Electronic Documents relates to the eDocument Cockpit

The eDocument Cockpit continues to support established electronic document processing. Manage Electronic Documents provides an SAP Fiori-based user experience with additional capabilities for monitoring and analyzing electronic documents.

Selected capabilities include:

  • Status overview with document counts
  • Visual process status flow
  • Document-level processing history, logs, and attachments
  • Dedicated Error Analysis

Watch the Demo

The short video below provides a practical walkthrough of the Manage Electronic Documents app for Türkiye and shows these capabilities in action.

 

Alternatively, watch the Demo on SAP Media Share.

Availability for Türkiye

In SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, Manage Electronic Documents and Error Analysis are supported for Türkiye.

At present, the app can be used by customers in Türkiye who use Sovos as their service provider.

With HFC 2608.2, support is planned to be extended to the service-provider-agnostic integration, allowing customers using other supported service providers to use the app as well.

Support for SAP S/4HANA and SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition depends on the corresponding framework and release availability.

Summary

The video provides a quick overview of Manage Electronic Documents and demonstrates selected capabilities in practice.

I hope the short overview is helpful. Feel free to share your feedback or questions in the comments.

entry.title: What Global SAP Teams Get Wrong About Peru: SIRE Is Not Another Report
entry.content:
If you are running an SAP project with a Peruvian entity in scope, there is a good chance your compliance workstream is sized incorrectly. Not because the team is careless, but because the requirement looks familiar and is not.

I have spent the last two decades working on ERP projects in Peru, mostly from the quality assurance side — the person who comes in and asks whether what was promised is actually what was built. Peru's electronic books requirement is, by a wide margin, the item I most often find underestimated in project plans written outside the country.

The change nobody reads carefully

For years, Peruvian companies filed their accounting books through PLE (Programa de Libros Electrónicos). The model was simple and familiar to anyone who has done statutory reporting: the company generates a flat file from its ERP, validates it, and submits it to SUNAT, the Peruvian tax authority.

Your system is the source of truth. You produce the book. You send it.

SIRE (Sistema Integrado de Registros Electrónicos) inverts that.

Under SIRE, SUNAT builds a proposal of your Sales Register (RVIE) and your Purchase Register (RCE) from the electronic invoices already in its own systems. Each period, the company receives that proposal and must accept it, replace it, or complement it.

Read that again, because it is the whole point: the tax authority now arrives with a version of your registers before you submit anything.

 

Why this breaks project assumptions

When a requirement is written as "generate and submit electronic books", a project team scopes a report. Development effort, a test cycle, a sign-off.

But SIRE is not a report. It is a reconciliation process that runs every period, between what your SAP system holds and what the tax authority already believes. That difference changes several things at once:

  • It is recurring operational work, not a one-time build. Someone in finance owns a monthly comparison and a decision on every discrepancy.
  • It exposes master data quality immediately. A supplier tax ID that never caused visible pain now produces a line that does not match.
  • It moves the deadline. The work no longer ends when the file is generated. It ends when the differences are resolved.
  • It needs a defined owner. In more than one project I have reviewed, the requirement sat between the finance team and the technical team, and neither had written down who decides what happens when the proposal and the ERP disagree.

None of this is exotic. It is simply a different shape of work than the one the plan was built around.

Where SAP sits in this

SAP covers Peru through SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, and there is a leading SAP Note for the country that is the correct starting point for any scoping conversation. My recommendation is boring and I will make it anyway: read the leading note before you estimate, not after. The gap between what the standard solution delivers and what the local requirement demands is where project timelines quietly go.

A note on timing

The transition has not been a single date. SUNAT has moved it more than once. Most recently, R.S. N.° 000392-2025/SUNAT postponed the obligation for principal taxpayers with 2024 net income above 2,300 UIT from January 2026 to June 2026, while taxpayers below that threshold stayed on the January date.

If your program plan was built on a schedule published a year earlier, it is worth checking which group your entity falls into. I have seen a team prepare diligently for the wrong month.

What I would tell a project manager

Three questions, and you will know whether this requirement is under control:

  1. Who, by name, reviews the SUNAT proposal each period and decides on differences?
  2. What happens when the proposal contains a document your ERP does not have?
  3. Has anyone run a full period end-to-end in a test environment, or has the team only validated that the file generates?

If the third question has no answer, the requirement is not tested. It is formatted.

entry.title: Hungary's Move to eVAT M2M
entry.content:
Most of you know: Hungary is retiring ÁNYK. The General Form Completion Program stops being usable for the VAT return at the end of 2026, and from 1 January 2027 the return has to go through the eVAT system instead. If you file VAT in Hungary, the tool you have been using for years stops working in a little over three months.

But here is the silver lining: SAP has already shipped most of what customers need. That is unusual for a legal change of this size, and it changes the question from “when can I start” to “why have I not started yet”? 

One point that gets mixed up easily

From 2027 the eVAT system is mandatory. eVAT M2M is not.

There are two ways into eVAT.:

1) The web interface, where NAV generates a draft return from the data it already holds and you review and adjust it
2) Machine-to-Machine (M2) channel, where your system sends the VAT analytics as XML through NAV's API.

The web route is simpler and usually suits smaller businesses better whereas M2M is built for high transaction volumes incl. cross-border and intra-Community data. Most SAP customers running Hungarian entities land in the second group, but it is worth saying out loud that the mandate is eVAT, and M2M is the option you choose.

The dates that matter

  • 1 January 2026. New VAT return structures took effect, including the new return package and ESPL form releases.
  • 1 August 2026. The eVAT 2.0 schema went live. NAV published it in mid-May, earlier than expected, which left the rest of 2026 for testing.
  • 31 December 2026. ÁNYK is discontinued for the base declaration and for any reporting period after this date.
  • 1 January 2027. Data-based channels only. The eVAT web interface or M2M.

The A60 form for intra-Community transactions moves into eVAT as well, once its schema is published.

Where SAP delivery stands

SAP Document and Reporting Compliance (link) is supporting customers for Hungary mandates. For current planned delivery dates and scope, please refer to SAP Regulatory Change Manager and select for SAP DRC and Hungary as country. (link: https://app.main.regulatory-change-manager.cloud.sap/index.html#/list=QWxs )

For planned timelines, please access tab ‘Product Impact’ and always refer back to RCM for current status of delivery and scope. You may also consider subscribing to the requirement to get notified of any updates instantly.

Two things that are easy to miss

  • The VAT coding has to line up with NAV's structure. This is usually where the work is, and it is a data and configuration exercise, not a technical integration one.
  • NAV changes the schemas. eVAT 2.0 arrived in 2026, and the cost of staying current is an ongoing one rather than a one-off project.

What is recommended now?

  • Check which SAP product and release your Hungarian entities run on, and match it against the delivery timelines in Regulatory Change Manager. If you are on S/4HANA in any flavour, the functionality is already there.
  • Decide between the web interface and M2M now, based on volume and on how much intra-Community activity you have.
  • Look at your VAT code mapping early. External advisers put implementation at one to two weeks for smaller companies and one to two months for larger ones, and most of that is data work.
  • Subscribe to Regulatory Change Manager and legal mandates listed for Hungary relevant for you to get notified instantly upon new updates  

Listen to SAP Experts

In a solution overview session for Hungary, local product managers of SAP Document and Reporting Compliance walk you through eVAT M2M process with SAP Document and Reporting Compliance: what the solution covers, how it works, and the steps to get ready. Here is the link to the recording and slides: https://event.on24.com/wcc/r/5462382/4AC703409D240B4C3B8FC7E2379B4DA3 (simply enter your email and the recording will start, PDF can be downloaded under additional resources section) 

More information:

Getting a Verification Code to Register Your Peppol Participant for Slovakia

Note: The steps and processes described here are accurate as of the time of writing, but it's essential to stay updated with any changes on the tax authority portal or the test tool for PFS that may affect this procedure.

If you are a Slovakian company and you use SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, cloud edition to exchange electronic documents with your business partners and the tax authority, you must register a Peppol participant for your company as part of the setup. One of the prerequisites for creating this participant is a verification code. The verification code confirms that you have selected SAP SE as your certified delivery service provider, making SAP your access point in the Peppol network.

How you obtain the verification code depends on whether you use it for production or for test purposes. In this blog, you will learn how to obtain the verification code for both.

Obtaining the Verification Code for Production Purposes

For production purposes, you obtain the verification code by registering on the Slovak Financial Administration portal and selecting SAP SE as your certified delivery service provider.

  1. Open the tax authority portal at https://vpds.financnasprava.sk/.
  2. Navigate to the page listing the accredited service providers.
  3. Choose SAP SE as your accredited service provider and initiate the registration of your participant by selecting the corresponding action in the portal.

After the request has been successfully submitted, the Financial Administration sends a message to your inbox in the Personal Internet Zone (Osobná internetová zóna – OIZ). The message is titled Submission of a request for selection of a certified delivery service provider (Odoslanie žiadosti pre výber certifikovaného poskytovateľa doručovacej služby).

  1. Inside this message, copy the Verification data / verification code (Verifikačný údaj): <#EncryptedData#> and use it as the verification code when creating the participant for your company for production purposes.

Important: If you have email notifications enabled, the notification e-mail only informs you that a new message has been delivered to your Financial Administration mailbox. The verification code itself is not included in the notification email — you must open the message directly in OIZ to retrieve it.

Obtaining the Verification Code for Test Purposes

For testing your integration with the Slovak Financial Administration's test environment (tPFS), you generate the verification code yourself using a dedicated test tool.

  1. Open the Test tools for PFS (Testovacie nástroje PFS) at overtoken.sk/generate. The page provides tools for testing integration with the Slovak Financial Administration test environment (tPFS).
  2. Sign in by clicking Sign in (Prihlásiť sa). If prompted, continue using the configured Google account.
  3. Scroll to the section Generate a standalone verification token (data) (Vygenerovať samostatný verifikačný token (údaj)).
  4. Enter the Service provider TIN for SAP (DIČ poskytovateľa služby): DE143454214
  5. Enter your Entity TIN (DIČ subjektu — 10 digits).
  6. Click Generate verification token (data) (Vygenerovať verifikačný token (údaj)).
  7. Copy the generated verification token and use it as the verification code when creating the participant for your company for test purposes.

Next Step: Creating a Peppol Participant for Slovakia

Once you have the verification code, you can proceed to create a Peppol participant for your company in SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, cloud edition. For more information, see Creating a Participant for Your Company for Slovakia.

entry.title: SAP DRC Cloud Edition para NF-e no Brasil: o que mudou em 2026?
entry.content:
SAP DRC Cloud Edition para NF-e no Brasil: o que mudou em 2026?

Em 2026, a SAP iniciou uma nova etapa na evolução de sua arquitetura de compliance fiscal eletrônico para o Brasil.

A nova integração de NF-e com o SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, Cloud Edition, apresentada pela SAP em fevereiro de 2026, consolida o direcionamento para uma plataforma global de comunicação fiscal eletrônica.

Até então, os cenários brasileiros utilizavam serviços específicos, principalmente o SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, outbound invoicing option for Brazil e o SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, inbound invoicing option for Brazil, cada um com sua própria estrutura de onboarding, comunicação e operação. Markdown colado

Com o SAP DRC Cloud Edition, esse conceito muda.

A estratégia passa a ser a utilização de uma plataforma cloud global, preparada para suportar diferentes países, documentos eletrônicos, processos de compliance e participantes externos.

Mais do que uma atualização de infraestrutura, estamos diante de uma mudança de arquitetura.

1. De serviços específicos para uma plataforma global

Uma das principais mudanças introduzidas pelo SAP DRC Cloud Edition é a centralização da comunicação fiscal.

A SAP posiciona o Cloud Edition como uma solução global para comunicação e submissão de documentos eletrônicos, permitindo que diferentes países e processos utilizem uma infraestrutura comum.

Entre os principais benefícios desse modelo estão:

  • padronização da arquitetura de integração;
  • estrutura global baseada em SAP BTP;
  • utilização de contas e subcontas;
  • simplificação do onboarding;
  • expansão para novos países e cenários;
  • centralização dos serviços;
  • monitoramento mais centralizado;
  • direcionamento das novas funcionalidades para o Cloud Edition.

A estratégia é resumida pela SAP no conceito:

One Solution Scalable Worldwide

Ou seja: uma solução global que pode ser expandida para diferentes países e obrigações fiscais. Markdown colado

A nova arquitetura pode ser dividida em três grandes componentes.

Business System: representa o sistema responsável pelos processos de negócio e informações fiscais, como SAP ECC, SAP ERP ou SAP S/4HANA.

SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, Cloud Edition: representa a camada cloud responsável pela integração, troca de documentos eletrônicos, comunicação fiscal e monitoramento.

External Communication Party: representa os participantes externos, como SEFAZ, outras autoridades fiscais, plataformas governamentais, redes externas e parceiros de negócio. Markdown colado

Portanto, de forma simplificada, passamos a trabalhar com uma arquitetura:

SAP ECC / SAP S/4HANA
↓
Integration Steps
↓
SAP DRC Cloud Edition no SAP BTP
↓
Autoridades fiscais / SEFAZ / Parceiros externos

2. O SAP BTP passa a ter papel central na arquitetura

Uma das mudanças mais relevantes é que o SAP BTP passa a fazer parte diretamente da arquitetura da solução.

O Cloud Edition não é simplesmente um novo endpoint para onde o ERP envia documentos.

É necessário realizar o onboarding e provisionamento do serviço no ambiente BTP.

Isso envolve elementos como:

Global Account → Subaccount → Entitlements → Service Plans → Subscription/Service Instance → Usuários e autorizações → SAP DRC Cloud Edition

Essa camada passa a ser fundamental para o funcionamento da solução.

3. Ativação e onboarding do SAP DRC Cloud Edition no BTP

A preparação do Cloud Edition começa no SAP BTP Cockpit.

A SAP disponibiliza um acelerador para auxiliar na configuração da conta do SAP DRC Cloud Edition.

O processo guiado permite executar etapas como:

 

1. Iniciar o acelerador - O administrador inicia a configuração da conta para SAP DRC Cloud Edition.

2. Verificar os pré-requisitos - O próprio processo valida pré-requisitos como autorizações e direitos de uso necessários.

3. Selecionar o cenário - É possível trabalhar com a criação de uma nova subconta ou selecionar uma subconta existente, conforme a arquitetura definida para o projeto.

4. Configurar a subconta - Nesta etapa são definidos elementos como o plano de serviço e a subconta que receberá os recursos necessários. É importante destacar que a arquitetura deve considerar adequadamente os ambientes de Teste e Produção.

5. Adicionar usuários - São definidos os usuários e respectivos provedores de identidade e autorizações.

6. Revisar e executar - O acelerador executa as atividades necessárias, como atribuição de quotas, assinatura da aplicação, criação das instâncias de serviço e atribuição das respectivas autorizações.

7. Validar a configuração - Ao final, a subconta fica preparada para utilização do SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, Cloud Edition.

Esse processo representa uma diferença importante na implementação: o onboarding da solução passa a fazer parte diretamente do desenho técnico do projeto.

4. Também existe a possibilidade de configuração manual

Além do processo assistido, os componentes podem ser preparados manualmente no SAP BTP.

De forma resumida, o processo envolve:

  1. criar a subconta na Global Account através do SAP BTP Cockpit;
  2. atribuir os respectivos entitlements, quotas e service plans;
  3. assinar/provisionar o SAP DRC Cloud Edition;
  4. atribuir usuários às Role Collections necessárias;
  5. criar a instância de serviço;
  6. obter as informações necessárias para integração com o Business System.

Essa possibilidade é particularmente importante quando o projeto exige maior controle da arquitetura BTP ou configurações específicas do ambiente.

5. Ativação do processo “Documentos fiscais eletrônicos (BR)”

Depois da preparação do ambiente BTP e provisionamento do Cloud Edition, é necessário habilitar o processo correspondente ao Brasil.

Dentro do SAP DRC Cloud Edition, o administrador acessa:

Configuração → Ativar processos e seleciona: Documentos fiscais eletrônicos (BR)

O processo inicialmente aparece como Inativo. Após selecionar Ativar, o sistema apresenta uma confirmação importante informando que, depois da ativação, o processo não poderá ser simplesmente desativado. Após a confirmação, o status passa para: Ativo

Essa etapa é importante porque habilita no tenant do Cloud Edition os recursos relacionados aos documentos fiscais eletrônicos brasileiros.

6. Um único ambiente de monitoramento no Cloud Edition

Outra evolução importante está no conceito de centralização do monitoramento.

No novo modelo, o SAP DRC Cloud Edition funciona como uma plataforma global para os diferentes processos suportados, permitindo uma visão mais centralizada da operação.

Em vez de pensar em soluções isoladas para cada país, o conceito passa a ser:

Uma plataforma global
↓
Diferentes países
↓
Diferentes processos fiscais
↓
Diferentes documentos eletrônicos
↓
Monitoramento centralizado

Isso é particularmente importante para organizações multinacionais.

Uma empresa pode evoluir sua utilização do DRC para outros países e obrigações fiscais utilizando a mesma estratégia global de plataforma.

No backend SAP continuam existindo os respectivos processos e ferramentas operacionais, como o eDocument Framework e EDOC_COCKPIT. Entretanto, a camada cloud passa a ser concentrada no SAP DRC Cloud Edition.

Essa distinção é importante: monitoramento centralizado no Cloud Edition não significa que o processamento de negócio do ERP deixa de existir.

7. Certificados digitais passam a ser administrados no ambiente Cloud Edition

Outro ponto fundamental da nova arquitetura é o tratamento dos certificados digitais.

A comunicação com as autoridades fiscais brasileiras depende dos certificados necessários para autenticação e assinatura, conforme o respectivo processo.

Durante a preparação do Cloud Edition, os certificados precisam ser disponibilizados e configurados no novo ambiente.

Portanto, a migração deve contemplar atividades como:

identificação dos certificados utilizados → exportação/preparação → validação da validade → validação da cadeia de certificação → carregamento/configuração no ambiente Cloud Edition → testes de comunicação.

Esse ponto deve fazer parte do planejamento desde o início.

Não basta configurar o ERP e estabelecer a comunicação com o BTP: o Cloud Edition também precisa estar corretamente preparado para se autenticar e se comunicar com as respectivas autoridades fiscais.

Isso também cria um novo ponto de governança.

A equipe responsável deverá controlar:

validade dos certificados, renovação, ambientes de Teste e Produção, empresas/CNPJs relacionados e configuração dos certificados no ambiente cloud.

8. SAP Note 3657680: ponto de partida técnico da implementação

Uma referência extremamente importante para a implementação é a:

SAP Note 3657680

Exchange of Electronic Fiscal Documents Using SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, Cloud Edition – Leading SAP Note

A SAP Note 3657680 orienta a integração dos processos Inbound e Outbound com o SAP DRC Cloud Edition e funciona como uma Leading SAP Note para o cenário.

Ela reúne e direciona para as SAP Notes, correções, pré-requisitos e soluções necessárias para habilitar essa integração.

Por isso, eu considero essa Note um dos primeiros pontos que devem ser analisados durante o assessment técnico de uma implementação.

Em vez de começar aplicando notas isoladamente, a recomendação prática é utilizar a 3657680 como referência principal e, a partir dela, identificar as notas correspondentes ao release e cenário do Business System.

Como as SAP Notes podem receber novas versões, pré-requisitos e correções, é importante consultar sempre a versão vigente diretamente no SAP for Me.

9. Integração entre ERP e SAP DRC Cloud Edition

Depois da preparação do ambiente cloud, precisamos integrar o Business System ao Cloud Edition.

Esse é outro ponto importante da nova arquitetura.

A conexão exige configuração de comunicação e autenticação no backend.

Em um fluxo utilizando OAuth 2.0, por exemplo, temos atividades como:

1. Criar a ligação de serviço no Cloud Edition = A ligação disponibiliza os dados necessários para que o sistema de negócio consiga estabelecer comunicação segura com o serviço.

2. Obter as credenciais = As informações da ligação são utilizadas para configurar o cliente correspondente no backend.

3. Criar o perfil OAuth 2.0 no SAP ERP/S/4HANA = O backend precisa ser preparado para autenticação contra o novo serviço.

4. Configurar as credenciais e validar a autenticação = Somente depois dessa etapa temos efetivamente:

ERP ↔ autenticação ↔ Cloud Edition

Por isso, problemas de comunicação no novo modelo podem envolver diferentes camadas.

Um troubleshooting passa a analisar algo como:

Processo de negócio
↓
eDocument
↓
Integration Step
↓
Configuração do backend
↓
OAuth / autenticação
↓
SAP BTP
↓
SAP DRC Cloud Edition
↓
Certificado digital
↓
SEFAZ

Essa visão ponta a ponta será cada vez mais importante para profissionais que trabalham com DRC.

10. A migração precisa ser planejada como um processo controlado

Para clientes que já utilizam os serviços anteriores de NF-e do SAP DRC, a mudança não deve ser tratada simplesmente como uma alteração de endpoint.

O próprio conteúdo técnico do projeto evidencia uma sequência de preparação, configuração, validação e cutover. 

De forma resumida:

Preparação do Business System
↓
Análise e implementação das SAP Notes
↓
Preparação do SAP BTP
↓
Criação/configuração da subconta
↓
Provisionamento do SAP DRC Cloud Edition
↓
Configuração de usuários e autorizações
↓
Carregamento/configuração dos certificados digitais
↓
Ativação de Documentos fiscais eletrônicos (BR)
↓
Integração ERP ↔ Cloud Edition
↓
Configuração dos parâmetros específicos do Brasil
↓
Preparação dos processos Inbound/Outbound
↓
Testes
↓
Cutover

Existe ainda uma restrição importante: os serviços não devem permanecer ativos simultaneamente para o mesmo processo Inbound ou Outbound durante a operação. Markdown colado

11. Cuidados específicos com NF-e e CT-e Inbound

Para o processo Inbound, existe um cuidado adicional antes do cutover.

As consultas utilizadas na distribuição de NF-e e CT-e precisam ser corretamente tratadas antes da mudança.

Temos:

EDOC_BR_MNG_DISTDFE – NF-e

EDOC_BR_MNG_DIST_CTE – CT-e

Antes da mudança, os documentos pendentes precisam ser recuperados para o backend. O relatório EDOC_BR_DISTDFE_RETRIEVE pode ser utilizado nesse processo. O objetivo é chegar ao cutover com Total Documents = 0. 

Esse procedimento evita deixar documentos pendentes no fluxo anterior enquanto o novo ambiente começa a realizar as consultas.

12. O NSU precisa continuar do ponto correto

Outro detalhe técnico extremamente importante é o NSU – Número Sequencial Único.

Antes da desativação da distribuição anterior, o Updated NSU deve ser preservado.

Na configuração do novo ambiente, esse valor deve ser utilizado como:

Initial NSU

Portanto:

Updated NSU anterior → Initial NSU do Cloud Edition

Isso permite que a distribuição continue a partir do ponto correto, evitando descontinuidade na recuperação dos documentos. 

13. Ativação do Cloud Edition no backend

Depois que BTP, Cloud Edition, certificados, comunicação e processos estiverem preparados, chegamos ao ponto de ativação no Business System.

A configuração é realizada através da:

NFECE_SWITCHES – Atualizar funcionalidades de documentos fiscais eletrônicos

Os principais switches são:

DRCCE_IN – Ativar edição na nuvem para nota fiscal de entrada

DRCCE_OUT – Ativar edição na nuvem para nota fiscal de saída

Esses switches determinam quais processos passarão a utilizar o Cloud Edition. Markdown colado

Por isso, considero essa etapa o verdadeiro ponto de virada do cutover.

Antes de ativá-los, precisam estar validados pelo menos:

BTP → Cloud Edition → processo Brasil → certificados → autenticação → comunicação ERP ↔ Cloud → documentos pendentes → NSU → eventos → testes técnicos → testes funcionais.

14. O que não muda: o processo de negócio continua no SAP

O Cloud Edition não substitui os processos de negócio executados no backend.

No NF-e Inbound, por exemplo, podemos continuar tendo:

Recebimento do XML
↓
eDocument
↓
Validações
↓
Identificação do fornecedor
↓
Associação do Pedido de Compras
↓
Inbound Delivery
↓
Entrada de Mercadorias
↓
Invoice Verification / MIRO
↓
Contabilização

Portanto, precisamos separar claramente duas responsabilidades:

SAP DRC Cloud Edition: comunicação, integração e compliance eletrônico.

SAP ECC / SAP S/4HANA: processamento do documento e integração com os processos de negócio.

O eDocument Framework continua sendo fundamental nessa arquitetura. Markdown colado

Conclusão

A chegada do SAP Document and Reporting Compliance, Cloud Edition para NF-e no Brasil representa muito mais do que uma alteração na comunicação com a SEFAZ.

Estamos falando de uma evolução para uma arquitetura:

global → centralizada → baseada em SAP BTP → padronizada → escalável.

O BTP passa a ocupar um papel importante no onboarding e provisionamento da solução; o Cloud Edition centraliza os serviços e o monitoramento cloud; os certificados digitais passam a fazer parte da configuração do novo ambiente; e a integração com o Business System passa por uma arquitetura própria de comunicação e autenticação.

Ao mesmo tempo, o eDocument Framework e os processos de negócio continuam no backend SAP.

Por isso, uma implementação precisa ser analisada ponta a ponta:

SAP ECC/S/4HANA → eDocument → Integration Steps → SAP BTP → SAP DRC Cloud Edition → certificados digitais → SEFAZ

E, para iniciar essa jornada tecnicamente, a SAP Note 3657680 passa a ser uma referência fundamental, reunindo e direcionando as SAP Notes e soluções necessárias para habilitar a integração Inbound e Outbound com o Cloud Edition.

Não estamos simplesmente mudando um endpoint.

Estamos adotando uma nova arquitetura para o SAP DRC.

Nos próximos conteúdos pretendo aprofundar as configurações do SAP DRC Cloud Edition para NF-e, incluindo SAP BTP, certificados, integração com SAP ECC/S/4HANA, NF-e Inbound, CT-e, eDocument Framework e troubleshooting de cenários reais de implementação.

entry.title: EDOC_ADAPTOR_CLOUD BAdI Implementation for RESTRICT_CANCEL
entry.content:
The following blog post is relevant only for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Please note that Developer Extensibility is required.

 

Use case:

You are trying to cancel a Billing Document in SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud, but the system prevents it with the error message "Document XXXXXXXX: Unable to cancel document; Cancel related eDocument first". Alternative Use Case could be, that the cancellation of a billing document is allowed, but you want to further restrict it.

 

Important Warning:

This BAdI should only be used for special case handling allowing the cancellation or if you want to further restrict the cancellation. Please understand the country process in detail before overwriting standard country logic with the BAdI. If for example an eDocument is submitted and accepted by the authority, an invoice cancellations is often not allowed - the correction then has to be done with an additional document like credit memo or an additional invoice. Please keep also in mind that using this BAdI method can lead to inconsistent business data in your system - e.g. accepted eDocument with cancelled invoice. In many country implementations it is allowed to cancel the billing document, when the eDocument is in cancelled state or you were able to delete the eDocument.

 

Implementation:

To implement the above requirement method "if_edoc_adaptor_cloud~restrict_cancel" in BAdI EDOC_ADAPTOR_CLOUD (enhancement spot ES_EDOCUMENT_CLOUD). The method “restrict_cancel” receives the edocument data in the importing parameter “is_edocument” and source key and source type. The changing parameter “cv_restrict” allows you to control whether the electronic document can be cancelled or not - the value which is handed over is the determined value by standard.

Implementation Steps:

  1. Create implementation for enhancement spot ES_DOCUMENT_CLOUD.
  2. Create BAdI implementation for EDOC_ADAPTOR_CLOUD.
  3. (Optional) Create BAdI Filter for Country and/or Generic Filter.
  4. Create implementing class for BAdI EDOC_ADAPTOR_CLOUD, which implements the interfaces "if_badi_interfaces" and "if_edoc_adaptor_cloud".
  5. Implement method "restrict_cancel" of interface "if_edoc_adaptor_cloud" in your BAdI class.
  6. Activate your BAdI implementation.
  METHOD if_edoc_adaptor_cloud~restrict_cancel.
      IF <your condition>.
        cv_restrict = abap_true/abap_false.
      ENDIF.
  ENDMETHOD.

entry.title: EDOC_ADAPTOR_CLOUD BAdI Implementation for CHANGE_EDOCUMENT_TYPE
entry.content:
The following blog post is relevant only for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Please note that Developer Extensibility is required.

 

Use Case:

The Standard SAP eDocument Solution determines the eDocument Type with the values defined in "Assign eDocument Type to Accounting Document Type/Billing Document Type/Delivery Type/…". There are situations, were it is not enough to define eDocument Type based on the source applications document type. In those situations, you can use the BAdI EDOC_ADAPTOR_CLOUD~CHANGE_EDOCUMENT_TYPE.

 

Hint:

Please search for notes before implementing this BAdI, if there is anything released. Sometimes, there is further customization possible to distinguish the eDocument Type. You could also check, if you can change your source application customizing to better distinguish.

 

Implementation:

To implement, use method "if_edoc_adaptor_cloud~change_edocument_type" in BAdI EDOC_ADAPTOR_CLOUD (enhancement spot ES_EDOCUMENT_CLOUD). The method “change_edocument_type” receives the source data in the importing parameter “is_source_data”, "iv_source_key" and "iv_source_type". The changing parameter “CV_EDOC_TYPE” allows you to change the eDocument type which is selected for creation.

Implementation Steps:

  1. Create implementation for enhancement spot ES_DOCUMENT_CLOUD.
  2. Create BAdI implementation for EDOC_ADAPTOR_CLOUD.
  3. (Optional) Create BAdI Filter for Country and/or Generic Filter.
  4. Create implementing class for BAdI EDOC_ADAPTOR_CLOUD, which implements the interfaces "if_badi_interfaces" and "if_edoc_adaptor_cloud".
  5. Implement method "change_edocument_type" of interface "if_edoc_adaptor_cloud" in your BAdI class.
  6. Activate your BAdI implementation.

entry.title: France Electronic Reporting via Approved Platform: An Overview of the Information Available
entry.content:
Hi everyone,
Many of you have already started working on the mandate for electronic invoicing and reporting reform for France, which introduces the mandatory digital invoice exchange and reporting of taxable transactions through an approved platform. 

In this blog post, I would like to share an overview of the information that's available for you when using electronic reporting via an approved platform. 

Legal Requirement and Scope 

France’s compliance reform is based on two pillars: electronic invoicing and electronic reporting. The scope of electronic invoicing covers domestic B2B transactions, payment data for services, and down payments for goods and services. Electronic reporting, by contrast, covers domestic and international B2C transactions, international B2B transactions (including exports, intra-Community supplies, and other cross-border transactions), payment data for services, and down payments for goods and services.

The determining factor is establishment in France for VAT purposes, rather than merely holding a French VAT registration number. Companies established in France may therefore be subject to both pillars. Foreign companies that are registered for VAT in France but are not established in France for VAT purposes have no electronic invoicing obligation. However, they may be subject to electronic reporting for transactions carried out in France for which they are liable for VAT.

For more information on the legal requirement and the announcement of upcoming deliveries for France Electronic Invoicing and Reporting, see SAP Regulatory Change Manager. 

 

More Information about New Features and Updates 

Implementation Overview SAP Note 

A starting point for checking the features that are made available is the Overview Implementation SAP Note. For the France mandate, there are two relevant overview SAP Notes: 

  • For electronic invoicing: SAP Note 3413565. 
  • For electronic reporting: SAP Note 3713986. 

Although our focus in this blog post is on electronic reporting, there are some technical dependencies with the electronic invoicing solution. Therefore, always check the prerequisites stated in the SAP Notes before implementing anything. 

What's New Topics 

For information on the new features being released, you can look for the What's New topics: 

SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition:

    Search for "approved platform" and review the What's New topics related to: 
  • Electronic Invoicing and Reporting via Approved Platform 
  • Electronic Reporting via Approved Platform 

SAP S/4HANA and SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition: 

  • What's New for Functional Localizations in SAP S/4HANA 
    Navigate to  France > Cross-Application Functions > Document and Reporting Compliance > Electronic Invoicing and Reporting via Approved Platform. 
    Review the What’s New topics related to: 
  • Electronic Invoicing and Reporting via Approved Platform 
  • Electronic Reporting  via Approved Platform 

 SAP ERP: 

  • What's New for Functional Localizations in SAP ERP 
    Navigate to  France > Cross-Application Functions > Document and Reporting Compliance > Electronic Invoicing and Reporting via Approved Platform. 
    Review the What’s New topics related to: 
  • Electronic Invoicing and Reporting via Approved Platform 
  • Electronic Reporting  via Approved Platform  

 

Product Documentation 

For information on the product features that are available, see: 

SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition:  

  • For an overview of the electronic invoicing and electronic reporting via approved platform, see Electronic Invoicing and Electronic Reporting via Approved Platform. 
  • For more information on electronic reporting, see Getting Started with Electronic Reporting. In this topic, you find all the relevant settings required for the solution.  

SAP S/4HANA and SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition:  

  • For an overview of the electronic invoicing and electronic reporting via approved platform, see Electronic Invoicing and Reporting via Approved Platform.
  • For more information on electronic reporting, Getting Started with Electronic Reporting. In this topic, you find all the relevant settings required for the solution.  

SAP ERP:  

  • For an overview of the electronic invoicing and electronic reporting via approved platform, see Electronic Invoicing and Reporting via Approved Platform. 
  • For more information on electronic reporting, see Getting Started with Electronic Reporting. In this topic, you find all the relevant settings required for the solution. 

Tip: The links above take you to the latest version of the documentation of that product. Depending on the release of your system, make sure you select the specific release to display the relevant information for your system release: 

 

 

WorkZone Group 

The WorkZone group is available to help the community address questions, learn from other experiences, and used to announce daily updates in case there's a known issue, for example, if the government system is down. See France - SAP Document and Reporting Compliance. Stay tuned! 

 

Troubleshooting and FAQ 

As we learn from your experiences and business scenarios, we gather that information and include it in SAP Knowledge-Based Articles. For France Electronic Reporting, see 3756217 - eDocument France via Approved Platform Troubleshooting Guide. 

If you haven't found information on the channels above, you can use the support channel and open a customer case to the following component: CA-GTF-CSC-EDO-FR-RE. 

Please read through the information that is provided first, and you can also use the Feedback option on the Help Portal to help us understand whether the information is helpful. Please leave your comment so that we learn what didn't go well when you looked for specific information - That will guide us to the next improvements.

 

Blog Posts 

In case you missed, colleagues have already published more information on the approved platform. See: 

  • Processing Electronic Invoices in France with SAP Document and Reporting Compliance 
  • Determination of electronic document processes in France with SAP Document and Reporting Compliance 
  • France E-Invoices and E-Reports: The Cloud Edition as Your Approved Platform 

 

We hope this gives you an overview of the different sources of information available to keep you informed on the latest updates for France. 

Stay tuned for upcoming blog posts on electronic reporting. 

Until next time, 

Ailane Kuhn

This blog post continues our series on France Electronic Reporting.

If you would like to understand the information that is available to help you navigate on the mandate, see France Electronic Reporting via Approved Platform: An Overview of the Information Available .

entry.title: France Electronic Reporting via Approved Platform: Key Differences Across Products and Releases
entry.content:
Hi everyone,


This blog post continues our series on France Electronic Reporting.

In case you missed the previous blog posts: 

  • See France Electronic Reporting via Approved Platform: An Overview of the Information Available for an overview of the information that is available to help you navigate on the mandate. 
  • See France Electronic Reporting via Approved Platform: Settings Checklist Based on Business Scenarios for a settings checklist based on business scenarios. 

In this blog post, I would like to share some differences across products and releases that are worth pointing out. 

 

Differences Across Products and Releases to Keep in Mind 

In SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition, SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition, SAP S/4HANA 2021 and higher, your entry point is the Run Statutory Reports app (App ID: F1515). For more information on statutory reports, see: 

  • SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition: Statutory Reporting 
  • SAP S/4HANA: Statutory Reporting  

Within the app, you select the report you want to run, and you can use the Manage Electronic Documents reporting activity that takes you to the Manage Electronic Documents app (App ID: F4306). You can use the Source for Invoice Reporting and Source for Payment Reporting processes to check the eDocuments that are created for a reporting period. You can also perform actions, such as change the tax reporting date of electronic documents before they are included in a list. 

Once you're ready, you can prepare the report run. Differently from lower releases, you check the statuses of the report submission within the Run Statutory Reports app, and once a report run is available, you can also show statutory reports from the Manage Electronic Documents app.  Note that the document status and report run status might not get updated immediately. Once a response is received from the authorities, you can view the response file in the document status log.

After a list has been submitted and accepted by authority, you can generate a rectification by starting a new phase if you want to add or remove an eDocument from a reporting period by changing the tax reporting date. Currently, to remove an eDocument from a list, you can post a credit memo with a reference to the initial invoice.  

Tip:  

  • You can use the Run Statutory Reports - France e-Reporting  app (ID: F1515_FR_4) to run the reports specific for France Electronic Reporting. For more information, see SAP Note  3721231 .
  • If you're new to using the Manage Electronic Documents app, you can find more information on the differences between the Fiori app and the Cockpit (available in lower releases) here: What are the differences between the Manage Electronic Documents app and eDocument Cockpit app? | SAP Help Portal. 

Remember: In Fiori apps, you can find more information about specific fields and process statuses when you select the Question Marc icon on the top right of the screen. A side panel displays more information about specific fields. 

For more information on the procedure to generate each report, see: 

  • SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition: Generating the Customer Invoice List, Generating the Supplier Invoice List, Generating the Payment List. 
  • SAP S/4HANA and SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition 2021 and higher: Generating the Customer Invoice List, Generating the Supplier Invoice List, and Generating the Payment List. 

 

In SAP S/4HANA 2020 and below, and in SAP ERP, you can use the eDocument Cockpit (transaction EDOC_COCKPIT) and the Source for Invoice Reporting (FRIVREPSRC) and Source for Payment Reporting (FRPYREPSRC) processes to display the eDocuments that are created for a reporting period. You can also perform actions, such as change the tax reporting date or cancel electronic documents before they are included in a list. 

Once you have the relevant eDocuments created for a reporting period, you run the Create Lists of Electronic Documents report (transaction EDOC_FR_EREP) to generate the lists. You then go back to the eDocument Cockpit (transaction EDOC_COCKPIT) and you use the processes Invoice Reporting (FRINVREP_E) and Payment Reporting (FRPAYREP_E) to display the lists that have been generated, submit them to the authorities, and check the report submission statuses. 

  • SAP S/4HANA 2020 and below: Generating Customer Invoice Reporting, Generating Supplier Invoice Reporting, and Generating Payment Reporting.  
  • SAP ERP: Generating Customer Invoice Reporting, Generating Supplier Invoice Reporting, and Generating Payment Reporting. 

After a list has been submitted and accepted by authority, you can generate a rectification if you want to add or remove an eDocument from a reporting period by changing the tax reporting date. Currently, to remove an eDocument from a list, you can post a credit memo with a reference to the initial invoice. For more information on the rectification, see: 

  • SAP S/4HANA 2020 and below: Correcting Data After Submitting the Customer Invoice Reporting to the Tax Authority, Correcting Data After Submitting the Supplier Invoice Reporting to the Tax Authority, and Correcting Data After Submitting the Payment Reporting to the Tax Authority.    
  • SAP ERP: Correcting Data After Submitting the Customer Invoice Reporting to the Tax Authority, Correcting Data After Submitting the Supplier Invoice Reporting to the Tax Authority, and Correcting Data After Submitting the Payment Reporting to the Tax Authority.     

 

We hope that this overview helps you find the information you need for the product you use and for your system release. Let us know if you have questions in the comments section below. 

Best regards, 

Ailane Kuhn

entry.title: UAE eInvoice: Capturing Down Payments and Prepaid Amounts
entry.content:
Overview

Down payments are common in many industries. When a customer pays a deposit upfront and then receives an invoice for the remaining balance, the UAE PINT AE eInvoice standard requires the invoice to explicitly declare the amount already paid. This is the prepaid amount field.

This post walks through the three main SAP process paths for handling down payments and explains how the prepaid amount gets captured in the XML eInvoice for each one.

The Prepaid Amount in PINT AE

In the PINT AE (Peppol International Invoice) standard adopted by the UAE, the monetary totals section of an invoice carries:

Term ID Name XML Element

IBT-112Invoice total amount with VATcbc:TaxInclusiveAmount
IBT-113Paid amountcbc:PrepaidAmount
IBT-115Amount due for paymentcbc:PayableAmount

The relationship is straightforward:

PayableAmount (IBT-115) = TaxInclusiveAmount (IBT-112) − PrepaidAmount (IBT-113)

A down payment invoice (the first document) carries the full down payment amount as its TaxInclusiveAmount with PayableAmount equal to that same amount and PrepaidAmount of zero.

The invoice references the down payment and sets PrepaidAmount equal to the down payment amount already collected, so PayableAmount reflects only the remaining balance due.

<!-- Invoice monetary totals example -->
<cac:LegalMonetaryTotal>
  <cbc:LineExtensionAmount currencyID="AED">10000.00</cbc:LineExtensionAmount>
  <cbc:TaxExclusiveAmount currencyID="AED">10000.00</cbc:TaxExclusiveAmount>
  <cbc:TaxInclusiveAmount currencyID="AED">10500.00</cbc:TaxInclusiveAmount>
  <cbc:PrepaidAmount currencyID="AED">2100.00</cbc:PrepaidAmount>
  <cbc:PayableAmount currencyID="AED">8400.00</cbc:PayableAmount>
</cac:LegalMonetaryTotal>

Scenario 1: SD Down Payment via Billing Plan

This is the fully integrated SD path. Down payments are modelled as a billing plan on the sales order, and every invoice — both the down payment request and the final delivery-based invoice — is created as a standard SD billing document.

Process Flow

VA01 | Manage Sales Orders (F1873)
Create Sales Order with Billing Plan (including Down Payment milestone)VA01 | Manage Sales Orders (F1873)
Create Down Payment Request (DP Request refers to SO and the DP Billing Plan)
VA02 | Manage Sales Orders (F1873)
Remove Billing Block on the DP Request
VF01 | Create Billing Documents (F0798)
Create Down Payment Billing Document → eDocument created (Down Payment Invoice)
VL01N | Manage Outbound Deliveries (F0867A) 
Create Outbound Delivery
VF01 | Create Billing Documents (F0798)
Create Billing Document (refers to Outbound Delivery) → eDocument created (prepaid amount captured)

How the Prepaid Amount Is Captured

When the final billing document is created in VF01 against the outbound delivery, SAP SD billing knows about the prior down payment billing document linked to the same sales order via the billing plan. The billing value calculation nets out the already-invoiced down payment amount.

The eDocument mapping reads the billing document's financial data — specifically the cleared down payment offset — and places this value into cbc:PrepaidAmount. The down payment billing document itself becomes the Down Payment Invoice eDocument (with PrepaidAmount = 0), while the final delivery invoice carries PrepaidAmount equal to the down payment value.

Key Points

  • The down payment billing document is submitted as a separate eDocument before the final invoice.
  • No FI posting is needed to trigger the prepaid amount: the entire lifecycle stays within SD billing.
  • The billing plan configuration (payment milestone type, percentages or fixed amounts) drives the down payment value.

Scenario 2: SD-FI Down Payment

In this scenario the sales order exists in SD, but the down payment is posted through the FI module directly rather than through a SD billing document. This is common when the down payment is handled by the finance department independently from the SD billing cycle.

Process Flow

VA01 | Manage Sales Orders (F1873)
Create Sales Order
F-37 | Post Down Payment Request – Customers (F1689)
Create Down Payment Request (optional; creates a noted item)
F-29 | Post Down Payment – Customers
Create Down Payment Document (optional, refers to DP Request) → eDocument created (Down Payment Invoice)
VL01N | Manage Outbound Deliveries (F0867A) 
Create Outbound Delivery
VF01 | Create Billing Documents (F0798) 
Create Billing Document (refers to Outbound Delivery) → eDocument created (should NOT be submitted yet)
F-39 | Clear Incoming Down Payments – Customers (F8969)
Clear Down Payment against the final customer invoice → eDocument updated with prepaid amount

How the Prepaid Amount Is Captured

The VF01 billing document triggers the initial creation of the eDocument, but at that moment the down payment has not yet been applied against the open receivable. The eDocument is therefore held — it should not be submitted to the tax authority at this point.

The clearing step (F-39) links the down payment posting to the open invoice item. After clearing, the eDocument framework detects the change on the underlying accounting document and updates the eDocument. The cleared down payment amount flows into cbc:PrepaidAmount, and cbc:PayableAmount is recalculated as the net amount due.

Only after F-39 is the eDocument ready for submission.

Key Points

  • The Down Payment Document from F-29 generates its own eDocument — the Down Payment Invoice submitted before the final invoice.
  • The final billing document eDocument must not be submitted before the F-39 clearing step.
  • F-39 triggers the eDocument update that populates PrepaidAmount.
  • F-37 (the DP Request) is a noted item and does not generate an eDocument on its own.

Scenario 3: FI Down Payment (No SD Sales Order)

This scenario applies to standalone financial transactions — service invoices, lease prepayments, or any situation where no SD sales order is involved. The entire lifecycle runs through FI.

Process Flow

F-37 | Post Down Payment Request – Customers (F1689)
Create Down Payment Request (optional; creates a noted item)
F-29 | Post Down Payment – Customers
Create Down Payment Document (optional, refers to DP Request) → eDocument created (Down Payment Invoice)
FB70 | Create Outgoing Invoices
Create Customer Invoice → eDocument created (should NOT be submitted yet)
F-39 | Clear Incoming Down Payments – Customers  (F8969)
Clear Down Payment against the customer invoice → eDocument updated with prepaid amount

How the Prepaid Amount Is Captured

The mechanism mirrors Scenario 2. FB70 posts the customer invoice and the eDocument framework creates an eDocument, but the document must not be submitted before clearing.

F-39 applies the previously posted down payment against the open invoice item. The eDocument is updated with the cleared amount as PrepaidAmount. The net PayableAmount reflects only the residual balance owed by the customer.

Key Points

  • F-37 creates a noted item only — no FI document, no eDocument.
  • F-29 generates the actual down payment posting and the corresponding Down Payment Invoice eDocument.
  • FB70 triggers initial eDocument creation, but submission waits for F-39.
  • F-39 is the event that finalises the PrepaidAmount on the final invoice eDocument.

Summary Comparison

 Scenario 1 (SD Billing Plan) Scenario 2 (SD-FI)Scenario 3 (FI Only)
Down Payment InvoiceVF01 billing documentF-29 postingF-29 posting
Final InvoiceVF01 billing documentVF01 billing documentFB70 posting
Prepaid Amount SourceSD billing plan nettingF-39 clearingF-39 clearing
eDocument hold required?NoYes (before F-39)Yes (before F-39)
Clearing step needed?NoF-39F-39

Submission Sequence

Regardless of scenario, the submission sequence to the UAE tax authority must always be:

  1. Down Payment Invoice eDocument — submitted first, confirms the advance payment collected.
  2. Invoice eDocument — submitted after the prepaid amount is cleared, carries PrepaidAmount and reduced PayableAmount.

Submitting the final invoice before the down payment invoice, or submitting the final invoice before the clearing step in Scenarios 2 and 3, will result in an invalid eDocument with a missing

or incorrect PrepaidAmount.

Fiori App Reference

Transaction Fiori App Name App IDVA01 Manage Sales Orders F1873VA02 Manage Sales Orders F1873VF01 Create Billing Documents F0798VL01N Manage Outbound Deliveries F0867AF-37 Post Down Payment Request – Customers F1689F-29 Post Down Payment – Customers  F-39 Clear Incoming Down Payments – Customers F8969FB70 Create Outgoing Invoices  

Confirm via the SAP Fiori Apps Reference Library.

Configuration Note

For the eDocument framework to correctly identify a billing document or FI posting as a down payment and map it to the appropriate PINT AE document type, the DRC process configuration for UAE must be active and the down payment process subtype must be correctly assigned. Verify this in the DRC Cockpit under the UAE country scope.

FI Document Type for Down Payments (Scenarios 2 and 3)

The FI document type assigned to down payment postings (F-29) must be different from the document type used for normal customer payment receipts. The eDocument framework relies on the document type to classify an incoming posting as a down payment and trigger the Down Payment Invoice eDocument. If down payment postings and regular customer payments share the same document type, the framework cannot distinguish between them — eDocuments will be created for both, causing regular customer payment receipts to incorrectly trigger eDocument generation..
